title: Business Security Partner (L5), Consumer & Content
description:
At Netflix, our mission is to entertain the world. Together, we are writing the next episode - pushing the boundaries of storytelling, global fandom and making the unimaginable a reality. We are a dream team obsessed with the uncomfortable excitement of discovering what happens when you merge creativity, intuition and cutting-edge technology. Come be a part of what’s next.

The Team

Netflix’s Business Security Partner (BSP) team is a team of senior security advisors organized around business proximity rather than technical domains. Each BSP partner owns relationships with a defined portfolio of business units, builds long-term relationships with BU leadership, and serves as the security export who understands those businesses well enough to advise on decisions before they are made. We sit in business reviews, participate in architecture conversations, and build the kind of trust with stakeholders that makes security a resource rather than a requirement.

Across all of our relationships, the goal is the same: every major business decision at Netflix should have access to clear, usable security risk context; not a compliance output buried in a document, but actionable guidance from a partner who understands both the risk and the business.

About the Role

This role covers two distinct and fast-moving areas within Netflix.  BSP aligns coverage based on need; BSPs also often rotate business units on occasion. You may cover other areas during your time at Netflix.

On the Customer Service side, you will be the primary security partner for a global support organization that is deploying AI capabilities across its consumer-facing operations. You will advise on the security risk of new technologies as they launch, help the organization assess and manage risk for systems that handle significant consumer data volumes, and maintain the overall security posture for a high-scale, globally operating support environment

For Content Generation, you will partner with teams that are building the next generation of GenAI / GenMedia production pipelines; prosperity models, open-source tools, and third-party inference providers running on CPU compute infrastructure to generate visual context for Netflix productions. Your work will span third-party AI tool evaluations, compute infrastructure security, training data governance, and security control decisions for AI-assisted content workflows. You will partner with multiple cross-functional teams to drive remediation of identified risks. The content these systems touch is pre-release Netflix IP, and the pace of change is high.

This role also carries M&A responsibilities. BSPs at Netflix are expected to support technical security due diligence for acquisitions and subsidiaries.

What You Will Work On:

•
Own the security partnership for Customer Service and Creative Technology, building stakeholder relationships, learning how these businesses operate, and translating that context into opinionated security guidance.

•
Lead security risk assessments and treatment strategies with cross-functional teams as they launch new capabilities and tools.

•
Evaluate and advise on the security posture of GenAI/GenMedia - third-party tool evaluations, open-source model assessments, compute infrastructure security, and training data governance.

•
Maintain and evolve the Business Risk Profile for each business unit, prioritizing and driving remediation of the risks that matter most.

•
Support M&A technical security due diligence for acquisitions and subsidiaries.

•
Develop reporting and metrics that communicate risk posture and business security initiatives to SPA leadership and business unit stakeholders.

Desired Background:

•
Experience with securing GenAI systems, customer-facing deployments, and/or content generation / ML pipelines. You understand what makes AI systems distinct from traditional software.

•
Broad security domain knowledge across application security, cloud security, identity and access management, and data governance. You are comfortable operating across all of them and know when to go deep versus when to synthesize.

•
Strong stakeholder partnership instincts. You build trust with the business by demonstrating that you understand their context, not just their security posture. You know how to translate a technical finding into a business decision, and back to the Security department for support.

•
Experience advising on security for consumer-facing systems, customer data environments, or high-scale operational technology.

•
Comfort with ambiguity and novel technology environments. You have a framework for reasoning under uncertainty and for making recommendations when the answer isn't fully known.

•
M&A or technical due diligence experience is a plus and not required.

Our new tier allows us to offer our members more choice in how they consume content, attract new members at a lower price point, and create a compelling path for advertisers to reach deeply engaged audiences. We are well into year four of our advertising journey with more exciting things to come!

Our Team

Our team is new yet faces the enormous ambition of building highly performant advertising systems and delivering high impact to our business by monetizing our incredible slate of content. As one of the newest entrants in the rapidly growing Connected TV advertising space, we seek to build unique value propositions that help us differentiate from the competition and become a market leader in record time.

The Ads Platform Engineering org builds advertising systems and integrations that power ad delivery using our world-class content delivery ecosystem. We use a number of Netflix investments and innovations to power our ads, a unique mix of client and server-side ad insertions, state-of-the-art content delivery systems, ad encoding recipes, content understanding and metadata, and more. We deliver ads in a manner that's thoughtful of our members' viewing experience and drive great outcomes for advertisers.

The Account Foundations team owns the accounts domain for Netflix Ads, i.e the system that defines who our advertisers are, what they're eligible for, and how they transact. It sounds like table stakes, but we don't have a lot of the moving pieces in place yet. Today, account data is scattered across systems, hierarchies are incomplete, and too much of what should be automated is still done manually. Every team building on top of advertiser data, such as sales workflows, media planning, programmatic integrations, and packaging, runs into these gaps. Our job is to fix that from the ground up and make sure it doesn't become a problem again, as the business scales.

We're working across four areas:

•
Core Accounts: We're rebuilding the account data model that can actually represent how advertisers and agencies are structured in the real world, representing HoldCo hierarchies, brand relationships, and multi-tier agency structures with strong governance being enforced. This also enables the creation of externalized APIs, allowing advertisers and agencies to view and manage their accounts as we move into a world of agenctic buying.

•
Account Intelligence: We're building the enrichment layer to identify who our advertisers are, where they spend their advertising budget, how they're structured, and whether our internal data matches reality.

•
Account Cohort and Verification Automation: Cohort assignment and identity verification are both manual today and both scale linearly with advertiser growth. Handling these problems at scale in an automated manner will be one of the key drivers of our long term success.

•
Spend Attribution: We are building an automated attribution engine to accurately map programmatic spend from DSPs and map it with the corresponding advertisers, agencies, and ad accounts across supply channels.

The work is foundational, which means it's both high leverage and high stakes, as well as a truly zero-to-one space. The architectural decisions we make now will be load-bearing for every team in Netflix Ads for years.
